swim.governs: Ladders and a slipway into deep water in two small coves on the west side of Tramore Bay. They face south-east, out across the bay: winds and swell from the south and south-east come straight in.
swim.deepBasis: The EPA's own description: the water at the Guillamene is "deep at all stages of the tide and so is suitable for confident swimmers only"; Newtown Cove has "access to the deep water via ladders and a slipway and a stony beach".
swim.tideNote: The tide doesn't decide whether you can swim here.
swim.lifeguard: The EPA lists no lifeguard at either cove.

tide.basis: The Marine Institute's predictions for its Dunmore East tide gauge, 12 km east, used as they are: no time or height shift. Its predictions for Dungarvan, 28 km west, put high and low water 10 to 12 minutes earlier, so at Tramore, in between and nearer Dunmore, expect the tide a few minutes earlier than shown.
